title: The Kav: how a line comes out of the point, a hiyuli that only makes an up and a down
overview:
Chapter 14 turns to the *Kav*, the line drawn from the *reshimu*, and first asks a general question. The *reshimu* is a point. The *tzimtzum* is no obstacle, since the whole infinite light was stuffed into that point, as a blueprint holds a whole house. But a point does not spread out at all: practically it seems a true *tzimtzum*, like one word that means all of Shakespeare. So how can a line, its very opposite, come out of it?

The answer is that the point is a *hiyuli*. Like clay, letters, or the ground without a seed, it does not spread out because it could become anything, not because it is held back. Points joined make a line, as a teacher breaks "math" into subjects, and a good student is a point only while he absorbs. The first line is short: it only makes an up and a down, one standard of measure like a single ruler for the whole house, and so it is called the *kav hamida*. Yet it carries the real light of the Essence, measured to the receivers.

sections.title: The Kav, and first the general question: it is the very opposite of the reshimu
sections.summary: After the light before the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*, the next stage is the *Kav*. First, in general: the *reshimu* is a point that hides everything and does not spread out at all, like a yud, while the *Kav* is drawn out and spreads.

blocks.text:
With the light before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* (the impression left after it) explained, the next stage in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) is the *Kav* and the *chut*, the line and the thread drawn from the *reshimu*. Like everything, it has to be understood in detail.

But first, in general, and in general there is a question: the *Kav* is the exact opposite of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: כי הנה הנקודה מורה ההעלם והסתלקות הכל, עד שלא נשאר רק כנקודה א'
phrases.en: All of the light, the whole infinite light, was all hidden, and all that was left was one point.

phrases.he: וגם נקודה או רושם זה מורה בחינת העדר ההתפשטות למטה דוקא
phrases.en: Also, this tiny little point that's left of everything that was there before is in a way that it doesn't spread out, because it's a point.

phrases.he: דהיינו ענין העדר ההמשכה וההתגלות לאורך ורוחב
phrases.en: It has no *hispashtus*, which means it doesn't have an *orech*, it doesn't have a *rochav*.
this looks like the letter yud,

phrases.he: שאין בו תוך וחלל כו' כידוע.
phrases.en: It's just a point, has no inside.

blocks.text: The point means that the whole infinite light, everything G-d could do and be, "even all the fishes He can create, and all the infinite flavors of bubble gum", was hidden, and only one point was left. And that tiny point does not spread out, because it is a point.

Relative to the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite) and everything before the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* is like a zero, a nothing, with all the light hidden in it. Compared to everything that comes out afterwards, it is completely infinite.

It has no *hispashtus* (spreading forth): no *orech* (length), no *rochav* (breadth), nothing in the middle. It looks like a yud, which is just a point with no inside, while all the other letters have more dimensions.

sections.title: The tzimtzum is no obstacle: everything was put into the point
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum* did not take the light away but stuffed all of it into the point, as a blueprint holds the whole house. So, on the contrary, the *reshimu* is the source of every revelation that comes after it.

phrases.he: דהיינו מה שנשאר בבחינת נקודה לבד,
phrases.en: which is that all the light was hidden in just one point,
It could be the opposite, it could be that there would be a revelation coming out from the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: So what is the real problem with the *reshimu*: why can it not be revealed? It is not the *tzimtzum*, which left only a point: the last two chapters explained that the light was not removed, which would be the *tzimtzum* *kipshuto* (literally); it was hidden in a point.

blocks.title: The blueprint, the thrown stone and the peace sign
blocks.text: Like a blueprint, which has the whole house in it, or a sign to remember, which has the whole intellect in it: totally hidden, yet all there. A thrown stone carries your power of movement, even your whole essence, "which is why if it kills somebody, then they'll kill you", G-d save us. A peace sign hints at the hippies' whole philosophy, "but it's really just two fingers." In writing you see only fingers twitching; even the writer does not see the *sechel* (intellect), yet it all comes through onto the paper.

So the *tzimtzum* is no problem. Had it taken the light away, we would ask how it could be revealed again. But it put it all in there, and on the contrary, that is why the *reshimu* can be the source of everything after it. The whole *koach* (power) of the *Ein Sof* is stuffed in it: "every flavor bubble gum, the last one", every song, every sight. As far as a *tzimtzum* into a *nekuda* (point) goes, a revelation could come out of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: מפני שמחמת זה יוכלל בו הכל
phrases.en: because since it had this type of a *tzimtzum*, everything was put into it.
just that it's in a very short and hinted way,
on the contrary,

phrases.he: זהו עיקר סיבת כל גלוי ההשפעה כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Because the *tzimtzum* was of this kind, everything was put into the point. It made it a point because it stuffed the whole infinity in, only **in a very short and hinted way**, like the mnemonic and the signs to remember.

**On the contrary**, this is the main cause of all the revelation. All the lights of the *hishtalshelus* are re-extracted from the *reshimu*, as the original *Gemara* was reconstituted from the *Mishna*, which had put it into a short form.

blocks.title: Frank Lloyd Wright's few notes
blocks.text: Or a blueprint. "What's this guy's name, the famous... Frank Lloyd Wright?" He puts down a few notes and a little drawing, and the whole house comes out of it: it is all there in a hidden way, and that is why it can come out.

blocks.title: A tool shed instead of Fallingwater
blocks.text: *Tzimtzum kipshuto*, where nothing could come out, would be if they hired him for Fallingwater and he decided: "Nah, I don't want to make them a beautiful, artistic building... I'm going to write them a blueprint for a little tool shed." There he actually left out a lot. Or if they offer him a lot of money and he says, "No, sorry, won't do it": he is holding back his wisdom, complete *tzimtzum*. Here nothing is lost; it is just put in a hidden way.
That everything was put into the point is the whole reason there can be the whole *gilui* (revelation) afterwards: it is all there.

blocks.title: The builders and the blueprint
blocks.text: How do they build the house? Frank Lloyd Wright did not stand there telling them what to do. The builders "could just be these stupid people that don't know very much. You know, they know how to bang in a nail and drill in a screw." They need no art or engineering; theirs is a *chachma* (wisdom) of the hands, not of the brain.

sensitivity.reason: Calls builders, as a trade, possibly "stupid people that don't know very much".
sensitivity.publishable: How do they build the house? Frank Lloyd Wright did not stand there telling them what to do. The builders do not need to know what he knew: they know how to bang in a nail and drill in a screw. They need no art or engineering; theirs is a *chachma* (wisdom) of the hands, not of the brain.

blocks.title: Whose house is it?
blocks.text: In fact they did better than he did: he drew it on paper, they built it. "It's not so hard to draw a nice house on paper, it's a lot harder to build a nice house." Nobody makes a big deal about the drawing. So why is it his house? He did not touch one brick. Because it came out in that shape only by following the blueprint he put his whole wisdom into. So his *etzem* (essence) is connected to it: "if it would have fallen down, they would have sued him for not being an engineer."

He puts all his wisdom into the blueprint, and then you do not need him anymore, until you want to change something. To change even one line you have to bring him back, because only he understands what everything is for and how it works together.

blocks.title: The palace that collapsed for one dot
blocks.text:
An architect made plans for a king's palace. Whether it was lost in copying or the builder did not care, one dot on the plan was never built. It stood for the central support beam through the whole structure, but from a bird's eye view it was just a dot, not the walls. They built the whole thing, and it collapsed. "It's just a little thing. It's a little dot. I did the main thing." If you are missing the central point that holds it all up, it does not matter how little it is. The builders do not have to understand why.

The blueprint is like the *reshimu*; the dot, though a dot, is not what is meant here.

sections.title: Yet the point does not spread out: how can a line come from it?
sections.summary: Practically, what is hidden in one point is not there for us, like a single word meaning all of Shakespeare, or a black hole. The beginning of the answer: a point and a line are not two opposites, because points joined together make a line.

phrases.he: אבל מה שמנקודה זו מורה העדר ההתפשטות לגמרי למטה
phrases.en: but since this point is in a way that it totally doesn't spread out to below,

phrases.he: לכאורה, זהו ודאי נקרא צמצום גמור ואמיתי
phrases.en: seemingly, this is a complete and true *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: להעלים ולהסתיר לבלתי יבוא האור למטה
phrases.en: that the light is being concealed and covered over so that it should not come below,

blocks.text: As far as the *tzimtzum* goes, then, a *gilui* afterwards is no problem. But since this point does not spread out below at all, everything stuffed into a point, it seems to be a complete and true *tzimtzum*: the light is concealed so that it should not come below, hidden from those below, not given to them.

blocks.title: A string around your finger, and Roy G. Biv
blocks.text: As if you put the intellect in code: it is all there, but nobody is ever going to get it. The *reshimu* is shorter than a blueprint, as if he put it all in one dot; nobody will build a house from one dot. To him it is a string around his finger; someone else sees no *sechel* there. "My very eager mother served us nine juicy pickles": unless you are told, you will never figure out it is the order of the planets. Roy G. Biv for the rainbow is shorter still, and then it gets down to one point, and you are never going to figure it out.

The *reshimu* has two aspects. Everything is there: the whole point of the last few chapters is that the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* but puts everything into the *reshimu*. And yet it is hidden completely. The first is no problem. But as for the second, though it is all there, "practically, for me, it's not there. I don't care if it's there, you know?"

blocks.title: One word for all of Shakespeare, and "math" on the board
blocks.text: Say we make one word that means all of the Shakespearean plays. You are never going to figure it out. Or the teacher writes "math" on the board: "That word has it all in it. Everything that you're going to learn in this class... for all of your years in school... Learn it well and you'll know everything you have to know." And he walks out. They are never going to figure anything out. It is all in there, but put down to one point, with no way to get it out.

So it seems to be a *tzimtzum kipshuto* after all. He was not hiding the light, only stuffing it into the point, but as far as we are concerned he is intentionally hiding it, making it so short that we are never going to figure it out.

blocks.title: Parents speaking another language
blocks.text: Like parents who talk to each other in another language so the kids will not understand: they are saying everything, but for the kids it is as if they are not. Or two scientists speaking jargon: to regular people it is totally hidden.

blocks.title: Why the Zohar was written so hidden
blocks.text:
Rabbi Chaim Vital writes in his introduction to *Etz Chaim* (the Arizal's Tree of Life) that the wisdom of the *Zohar* was supposed to stay hidden until right before *Moshiach*. So why was it allowed to be written? Because it was written so hidden that it is as if it was not written; open it, even with commentaries, and you see that, until now.

Then why write it at all? Because right before *Moshiach* they will learn how to open these wisdoms up, so it was written for them. And we are at that time now: all the Kabbala, the secrets of the Torah and *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) are really written for us.

phrases.en: if so, that it's totally in a way of a point,
How does the *Kav* come out from the *reshimu*?
the *Kav* is the opposite of this,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת המשכה והתפשטות דקו כו'.
phrases.en: that *Kav* means a revelation and *hispashtus*.

blocks.text: If it is totally a point, how can its very opposite come from it? The *Kav* is *hamshacha* (drawing down) and *hispashtus*, revelation and spreading out. The *reshimu* seems a complete *tzimtzum* for the *Kav*: it is all there, but it is not letting it out.

blocks.title: Worse than a black hole
blocks.text: It seems like a black hole. "Oh, we'll go with a spaceship, and we'll pull out some stuff," and the more they try to get out, the more they get sucked in. That is the infinite power of *gevura* (might, restraint) in the *tzimtzum*, condensing everything into one point. Even more than a black hole, which has some size: our whole solar system made into a black hole would be the size of a bowling ball. G-d can make an infinitely small point and put everything in it.
And that is only the physical. This is much more than the physical; the whole physical world is like nothing. "The whole physical world is just made from angel poop, you know."

sensitivity.reason: Calls the physical world "angel poop", a crude image.
sensitivity.publishable: And that is only the physical. This is much more than the physical: compared to it, the whole physical world is like nothing at all.

blocks.text: G-d can take the whole *Ein Sof* and put it into one point, smashed in so tight that you are never going to get it out. So how do we get it out?

phrases.en: it's known,
the truth is,
that a point and a line are not two opposites.

phrases.he: שהרי הקו נמשך מן הנקודה, ומחיבור נקודות יחד נעשה קו כו'.

blocks.text: Now the beginning of the answer. **It's known** that in **truth** a point and a line, the *reshimu* and the *Kav*, are not two opposites, for points joined together make a line. You put a point, another next to it, and another, "and voila, they make a line... Ever learned geometry? Line is defined as a series of points."

blocks.title: The teacher breaks "math" into points
blocks.text: The teacher who wrote "math" on the board, had he stopped there, would leave them knowing nothing. But he breaks the point into points: arithmetic, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, calculus. They still know nothing, but they see math has parts. Arithmetic becomes addition, subtraction, multiplication and division; addition becomes whole numbers, fractions, decimals, negatives. "Okay, so now today we're going to just focus on one of these little sub-points." Then examples: 1 and 1 is 2, 2 and 2 is 4. Each is one point within the general point. He is still only giving them points, but eventually they have enough to connect the dots, read between the lines, and see the whole picture: they *chap* (catch) what you are trying to say.

So with words: each word alone is a total point, with no intellect to be seen in it. How are you supposed to know what "math" means? But given a few points as context, your mind reads between the lines, connects the dots and makes a line, for really you cannot make a line out of points.

blocks.title: In parentheses: a point has no dimensions
blocks.text: "In parentheses", and if you do not know some geometry, ignore this: a point has no dimensions. It is infinitely small, so however many you put together it is still zero and never becomes a line. A line is a higher thing; points can describe it, but something has to fill in the gaps. So too, a language of one word would not express enough, but a whole bunch of words can carry an idea.

blocks.title: The dots of a printed picture
blocks.text: A point alone floats in nothing: no context, no clues, you cannot tell up from down. But a printed picture, in some styles of printing, is all dots, and from far away your mind sees no dots, only a continuum, because it has enough to connect them and fill it in. So something revealed in points comes out as a line. There are really two things that come together, but that is more advanced. "But okay, end of parenthesis."

The basic idea: put a bunch of points together, point after point with a pen, and it makes a line. "We're not getting into like ultimate definitions of points right now, unless you want to, then you can read the parenthesis."
The general answer, then: a point and a line are not opposites. He does not say a line comes from the points themselves, but from connecting a bunch of points; something has to connect them.

sections.title: The point is a hiyuli: it does not spread out because it could become anything
sections.summary: The point is to the line as a *hiyuli* (raw potential) is to its spreading out. Like a child's talent for music, clay, bricks, letters, the ground without a seed or the power of intellect, it does not spread out because it is above spreading out and can become anything, not because it is held back.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא כידוע שהנקודה הוא כמו בחינת ההיולי לגבי הקו
phrases.en: that the *nekuda*, the relationship of the *reshimu* to the *Kav*, is like the relationship of a *hiyuli* to the *hispashtus*.

blocks.text: The answer, as is known: the *nekuda* is to the *Kav* as a *hiyuli* (raw potential) is to its *hispashtus*. Of a *hiyuli* we asked, is it there or not? In a way it seems not to be there.

blocks.title: Mozart's symphonies in a little kid
blocks.text: A person's *hiyuli* is his talent for music. When Mozart was a little kid, were all his symphonies in it? "Yeah, they must all be there because or else where did it come from?" Then why could he not just write them all out? Because they were totally hidden, not there as a *metzius* (an existence) at all, and he had to work to get them out. So too the *reshimu*: it is all there, but totally hidden.
But that it is totally hidden there does not mean it cannot come out. It is hidden because it is the essence, the source of everything.

blocks.title: The ground needs a seed
blocks.text: The ground will not grow without a seed, not because it cannot grow but because it could grow anything. It needs to be contracted to one plant, because it is too infinite. So with the power of movement or of sight: they are not held back; they are too infinite.

blocks.title: A one-dot caricature
blocks.text: Put a dot on paper: "Okay, there, that's my caricature. Guess who it is." You can't. A caricature needs only the main defining details, but one point is still too infinite: it could be a picture of anything, depending on where the other points go. Put them in, and you connect the dots, fill it in in your mind and get the picture. So with the *Kav*: the one point could become any line, and the lines any shape.

phrases.he: וכמו כל בחינת היולי או חומר פשוט
phrases.en: like any *hiyuli* or any simple matter,

phrases.he: שאף על פי שהוא בהעדר ההתפשטות דוקא,
phrases.en: even though it doesn't spread out,
it's not necessary that it can't spread out,
rather it's just, this is the nature of a *hiyuli*,

phrases.he: מפני שהוא למעלה עדיין מבחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: it's still higher than spreading out.
and that's why, since it's still the essence, it doesn't go down from its essential state.

blocks.text: **Like any *hiyuli* or any simple matter, even though it doesn't spread out**, that is not because it cannot. **This is the nature of a *hiyuli***: **it's still higher than spreading out.**

blocks.title: Clay, bricks and letters
blocks.text: What is in clay? In a way nothing, not because you cannot make something out of it but because you can make anything. And, "no pun intended", that is the point: even once you make something, the clay stays clay, the essence it is made of. Bricks do not change in a building; only the shape changed, and you can take it apart and use the same bricks for something else.

blocks.title: The same letters, a different book
blocks.text: So with letters: the same letters rearranged make a different book, as bricks in one order make a house, in another a barn or a wall. You see no intellect in letters not because they cannot express ideas, but because they are the essential building block that can express any idea. They stay that essence; how it is revealed comes only from their order.

So G-d put His whole *etzem* into the *reshimu*. Bring out just this one *hishtalshelus*? "What do you mean? G-d could do anything!" From the side of the *reshimu*, every one is there. But when He makes a number of points, we connect the dots, and the light is revealed only within the imaginary lines between them, as one certain thing. The points stay points: **since it's still the essence, it doesn't go down from its essential state**.

phrases.he: וכמו היולי של חיות החי בגלוי,
phrases.en: like the *hiyuli* of the lifeforce, like the consciousness of a living thing,
the way it's still included in the essence,
that it doesn't spread out to enliven, nor to be any consciousness.
like the *hiyuli* of movement, the way it's in the essence
before it spreads out to move.
like the power of growth,
before it grows something.
or like the power of the intellect,
before it spreads out to intellectualize, to come up with ideas.
so too, there are many other examples of this type of *hiyulim*.

blocks.text: **Like the *hiyuli* of the lifeforce**, the consciousness of a living thing, **the way it's still included in the essence**. That your power of consciousness, as it is in your soul, does not come out to seeing or hearing is not because it cannot. It is the essence, always there: that you are just alive.
**Like the *hiyuli* of movement, the way it's in the essence before it spreads out to move**: it is not moving not because you cannot move, but because you can move in any way.

blocks.title: Dirt without a seed
blocks.text: Or **the power of growth, before it grows something**. "I want to grow an apple tree. So I'm going to go get me some dirt." He waits and waits, and nothing grows, not even weeds. "I took the same dirt from that same place." Yes, but you need a seed, or it will not know what to grow. "Oh, so then I just need the seed, great... I don't need the dirt." No: the dirt is what grows it. "The seed just tells it how to grow."

**Or like the power of the intellect, before it spreads out** to come up with ideas: he could understand anything, each according to his ability. That no idea is coming out now is not because he cannot. **There are many other examples of this type of *hiyulim***: any essence, music, dancing, any talent, is like that.

phrases.en: it's understood,
this lack of *hispashtus*,
is not called a true *tzimtzum*,
from itself.
on the contrary,

phrases.he: הרי הוא כח ההיולי העצמי שממנו נמצא הכל בהתגלות והתפשטות
phrases.en: it is the essential *hiyuli* from which everything is found and spreads out.

blocks.text: So **this lack of *hispashtus* is not called a true *tzimtzum*, from itself**. It is not held back. The ground is not saying, "No, I'm not going to grow." **On the contrary**, **it is the essential *hiyuli* from which everything is found and spreads out**: "Here, I'll grow anything... Just tell me what, I'm ready... Tell me, I'll do it."

sections.title: So too the point and the line: the student who absorbs before he teaches
sections.summary: The point does not spread out only because the whole essence is in it, and the very fact that it is a point shows this. Like a good student who makes himself a point while he absorbs and will not talk in class, it is from this contraction that all the teaching comes afterwards.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא יובן בבחינת נקודה לגבי הקו
phrases.en: so too, the *nekuda* compared to the *Kav*.

phrases.he: שהעדר התפשטותה הוא רק מצד היותה בבחינת העצמיות שלמעלה מבחינת ההתפשטות עדיין
phrases.en: the only reason that the *reshimu*, the *nekuda*, is not spreading out is because it's still the essence that's higher than spreading out.

blocks.text: **So too, the *nekuda* compared to the *Kav***. The whole power of the Essence is in it, ready to bring out any *hishtalshelus*; G-d just picks which one, and that is the *Kav*. In the *reshimu* it is totally hidden, but put some more dots there and it reveals according to how you put them: as the *Kav* goes, so it reveals.

**The only reason that the *reshimu*, the *nekuda*, is not spreading out is because it's still the essence that's higher than spreading out**, the essence of all that could come out in this line. Though it came from everything being contracted to one point, with no revelation, **the very fact that it's a point shows that the whole essence is there**.

**And therefore, it's not coming out to be revealed below**: everything is there, so it is not revealed as one particular thing, like ground that can grow everything and so shows no particular plant. "Yeah, well we're not talking about that kind of a point." The point meant is the one in his next *mashal*.

phrases.en: like the *mashal* of a student,
sitting before his teacher,
that when he's trying to absorb the teaching of the teacher,

phrases.he: ונעשה כנקודה בצמצום כל עצמותו כו',
phrases.en: where he makes himself like a point, totally focusing his whole being,
he will not spit out,
like, let's say, to teach to somebody else, spreading out.
however,
after he receives from the teacher,
the opposite,
This very *tzimtzum*, this very fact that he was so focused

phrases.he: הוא שנמשך ממנו כל ההשפעה והתפשטות לזולתו כו'

phrases.en: as explained elsewhere.

blocks.title: The good student who says "Not now"
blocks.text: **Like the *mashal* of a student, sitting before his teacher**: absorbing, **he makes himself like a point**, his whole being contracted, and **he will not spit out** to anyone else. The good student, who will help you with homework and be a teacher one day, will not talk to you in class at all. "Hey, what did the teacher just say?" "Not now, not now." Why not, if he wants to teach it? Because right now he is absorbing it.

That is why he is a good student: listening, he is totally focused. Some say for this reason it is better not to take notes in class, only after it. Taking notes, you are not putting your whole self into listening, "because that's already spitting out." A student cannot spit out while he absorbs, or he will not absorb.

blocks.title: Focused like a point
blocks.text: Focused on one point, you cannot look out the window or think about playing baseball outside. "Oh look, he's being so mean, he doesn't want to teach anybody." No: he wants to teach everybody, and that is why he makes himself a point, so he can explain it afterwards.

blocks.title: The teacher who stops to think
blocks.text: Or the teacher himself, in the Rebbe's *mashal*: when he gets a new idea he stops teaching for a second, goes up to it and makes himself like a point. He is not contracting himself to hide from the students; he is getting the idea so he can bring it down to them, because he really wants to give to them.

The Rebbe says the same of the Frierdiker Rebbe: he is going up, in a way hidden from us, but that itself is a *gilui*. It shows how much he cares about the students, going up to get them this; and so he is going to bring down the *gilui* of *Moshiach*.

**However, after he receives from the teacher, the opposite**: from this very *tzimtzum*, the fact that he was so focused, talked to nobody in class and did not even think for himself about what he heard, comes all his giving and spreading out to others.

Listening to a teacher, you are not supposed to think about what he says, figure out how it fits with other things or interpret it. Take it in in its pure state, the facts as he says them, as you follow a story someone tells you. "That's the best way to learn." Afterwards you sort it out and work on it on your own. Someone who learns like that becomes a very good teacher, and it really sticks with you. **As explained elsewhere**.

phrases.en: from all this understood,

phrases.he: שהקו הנמשך מן הנקודה הוא רק כמו בחינת התפשטות מן היולי העצמי
phrases.en: the line that comes out from the point, that relationship is like the spreading out from a *hiyuli*.

blocks.text: **From all this understood, the line that comes out from the point** is like **the spreading out from a *hiyuli***. The *nekuda* stays hidden, but that does not stop the revelation; it is its source. The *reshimu*, being infinite, is never totally revealed, while the *Kav* reveals only one *hishtalshelus*. Still, everything in the *hishtalshelus* comes out from the *reshimu* through the *Kav*.

That the whole *reshimu* is never revealed does not stop anything you want from being revealed from it. It is a *hiyuli*, and "I mean, G-d could do it", but you cannot reveal infinity one line at a time. "It's too big of a zero."

As they say: a guy keeps saying, "I'm a nothing, I'm a nothing," and another says, "Look who thinks he's a nothing. I'm a bigger nothing." So the *reshimu* is a nothing, but a bigger nothing than our whole world.

sections.title: The short line: a hiyuli for length and breadth that makes an up and a down
sections.summary: As the point is a *hiyuli* for the line, so the short line is a *hiyuli* for the length and breadth of an area. It explains nothing in particular; it only makes an up and a down, a giver and a receiver, like the order of subjects in school, and that, says *Etz Chaim*, is its whole purpose.

phrases.en: however,
why is the *Kav* revealed in a way of like a short line?
it's explained elsewhere,

phrases.he: שכמו שהנקודה בחינת היולי לגבי הקו,
phrases.en: just like the point of the *reshimu* is a *hiyuli* compared to the *Kav*,

phrases.he: כך הקו בחינת היולי לבחינת אורך ורוחב דשטח
phrases.en: So too, a line is a *hiyuli* for a length and a width.

blocks.text: Another point, "a new paragraph": why is the *Kav* drawn as a *kav katzar* (a short line)? **It's explained elsewhere, just like the point of the *reshimu* is a *hiyuli* compared to the *Kav***, the line is a *hiyuli* for the length and breadth of a *shetach* (an area). Points together make a line; lines together draw all kinds of neat little shapes. The same line done over and over draws any shape, as the line is the same point done over and over, so in the big picture the line is kind of like a point.

What is the difference between a line and a point? A point has no context: no dimensions, no up or down, no right or left; it is just there. A line already shows a direction. You may not know which way it points, since the paper could be turned, but you see a polarity, ends going opposite ways. That essential difference is the point here: the whole *inyan* (matter) of the line is to make an up and a down.

That is why the kabbalists compared the *Kav* to a line, for this relationship of point and line. It is not really a line: "It's not like the upstairs is lines and points and, you know, G-d's like drawing with a compass and a pencil." Nor is it physical light coming down in a line. It is a *mashal*; everything eventually has to be translated into how it is in us.

phrases.en: it's known,
the line,

phrases.he: הגם שהוא בא בבחינת המשכה והתפשטות מלמעלה למטה,
phrases.en: even though a line is already spreading out from up to down, it's already drawn out,

phrases.he: אבל אינו ענין פרטית אופן המשכה כלל
phrases.en: It's not a particular way of *hamshacha*,

phrases.he: רק מה שנמשך האור מלמעלה למטה בלבד
phrases.en: it's just the idea of light of going from up to down.

blocks.text: **It's known, the line, even though a line is already spreading out from up to down, it's already drawn out**, is no particular way of *hamshacha* (drawing down) at all, **just the idea of light of going from up to down**. What does that mean?

blocks.title: The order of subjects in school
blocks.text: The teacher, as said before, breaks the point of math he wrote on the board into arithmetic, algebra, geometry and calculus, and arithmetic into addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. He keeps breaking it up.

blocks.title: Five oranges and one fishy
blocks.text: That is breaking the point of math into a hierarchy of more basic ideas. Little kids starting math, before adding five and eight, are just counting things: a picture of five oranges, and they circle four, five or six. Then adding: "one fishy and one fishy and that equals two fishies." Later come the more advanced things.

So there is already a whole hierarchy of up and down: a line broken out of a point. But the line still explains none of those subjects. It only orders math so you can see what level a person is on and what to teach him, as grades and a class plan for each year do: "okay, so if you're here on the line, now we're going to talk about this part of math." It is not yet an explanation of anything.

The actual explanation is like the *shetach* that comes out from the line. But first the point has to be broken into a line, because to someone who really knows math, arithmetic is not more basic than calculus; "they're all the same." To make it simple, you decide on a beginning and an end and put it in order.

So too *Chassidus* is in the way of circles, no beginning or end, really one point. "You can't really explain, you have to get it." Yet it has to be learned in order, and the advice is to start with the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds) as explained in *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity). So says a letter of the Frierdiker Rebbe, quoting the Rebbe Rashab in the name of the *Rebbe Maharash* (the fourth Lubavitcher Rebbe).

It is a tradition of the Chabad Rebbeim: *Chassidus* has no beginning and no end, so how do you ever jump in? There is a way in, the only book written in a line, *Shaar HaYichud*, straight from up to down. In all the others you are floating, a point in the middle of nowhere with no context. The real *kavana* (intention) is to learn the other books and get the *etzem*, but first you do this line, the *seder hishtalshelus* from up to down.

phrases.he: שעל ידי זה נמצא בחינת מעלה ומטה מהמשפיע אל המקבל
phrases.en: This creates the idea of up and down from the *mashpia* to the *mekabel*,
but in the *hiyuli* of the point,

phrases.he: אין בו מעלה ומטה, ראש תוך וסוף כו' כידוע
phrases.en: there's no up, down, beginning, middle, or end.
this is what it says in *Etz Chaim*,

phrases.he: דכל עיקר הארת הקו אינו רק להיות בחינת מעלה ומטה כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: The whole purpose of the line is to create the idea of up and down.

blocks.title: The ladder up to the diploma
blocks.text: **This creates the idea of up and down from the *mashpia* to the *mekabel***, the giver and the receiver: the teacher on top, the student at the bottom, and a ladder between them. First you learn this, then that, closer and closer until they give you a diploma and say now you can be a teacher. That is all the *Kav* is: making the system of measurement.

**But in the *hiyuli* of the point** it is not so. The line too is a *hiyuli*, but it has an up and a down. It is a *hiyuli* for any class plan: on any day you know what to teach by where they are, "as soon as we learn this, we'll learn that." It can come out in infinite ways, and each step can be explained with different examples; going off into a width, each teacher and each class goes differently.

But the line stays the same. No two years are the same, even with the same teacher, yet everybody climbs the same ladder: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, then algebra, geometry, trigonometry, calculus. Each step can come out in different ways, a width, but the line is the same. "I mean I'm not saying it has to be done totally that way, but let's say there's a standard, which there pretty much is."

Change the point and write "science" on the board, and it is a different class with its own line. But within a line you know which grade you are in, and if you come in mid-year, behind the class, you know where you are supposed to go: there is an up and a down.

But in **the *hiyuli* of the point, there's no up, down, beginning, middle, or end**. "Listen guys, math, you just got to get it. Either you got it or you don't. I got it and you don't, there's nothing you could do about it." It is all or nothing, so at that level teaching it is not even discussed.

With a line you have not taught anyone yet, but you have already thought of a student and that you will have to bring it down, to any student, with your system of what to teach ready. In the point you are not ready for anybody; to make it teachable takes this whole process of *tzimtzum*. "I just got it, I know it. It's all one point by me... and I can't express it to you." How do you add? "You do it, come on. Everybody knows that." You cannot tell that to a kid.
**This is what it says in *Etz Chaim***: the whole shining of the *Kav* is only to make an up and a down, as will be explained. **The whole purpose of the line is to create the idea of up and down**.

sections.title: One measuring rod for the whole house, three lines for every letter
sections.summary: You do not buy a stick for every length: one ruler, the smallest unit, measures out any house, and three lines make an A, an N or a Y. So the short line, which only makes up and down, is a *hiyuli* for every measure and every letter.

phrases.en: like a measuring rod

phrases.he: שאינו בא בגדר שטח הבנין עצמו, לאורך ורוחב
רק שבו מודד כל מדידת אורך וכל מדידת רוחב
phrases.en: but with the same measuring stick you measure every length and every width.

phrases.he: והוא עצמו רק כמו קו הקצר
phrases.en: and all it is is a little line, little stick,

phrases.he: שכולל כל אופני מדידות של אורך ורוחב כו'
phrases.en: and in this stick is hidden all possible combinations of lengths and widths,

blocks.title: A 150-foot measuring stick
blocks.text: **Like a measuring rod**, which is not part of the building's own length and breadth. Say the house is 150 feet by 100, three stories, "I don't know, how tall is that, let's say 45 feet", rooms of 10 by 12 and 8 by 6, then doorways, trim, windows. Do you go to the measuring stick store and buy a 150-foot stick, a 100-foot stick, a 10-foot one and a 12-foot one? "No, that's ridiculous." You get one measuring thing and use it for the whole thing.

blocks.title: One ruler for the whole house
blocks.text: You buy one yardstick, one ruler, and put it down again and again until you have 100 feet; with inches marked, you measure inches too. All you need is the smallest unit you will ever need, multiplied over and over. So the *Kav* only has to create up and down. Once the smallest unit of up and down is made, it is a *hiyuli* for measuring any *shetach*, in any direction, of any size, with no separate stick for each thing.

**But with the same measuring stick you measure every length and every width**, over and over. "It's a magic *hiyuli* measuring rod. You know, people say we don't have magic stuff. We have magic *hiyuli* measuring sticks." Like a genie in a bottle: "Amazing. *Hiyuli* powers."

**And all it is is a little line, little stick**, **and in this stick is hidden all possible combinations of lengths and widths**. Creating the *Kav* creates a system of up and down and right and left by which anything can be measured. But nothing is measured yet; it is not an actual *hamshacha*, only the ability to measure. It is still *hiyuli*, still infinite.

blocks.title: The lesson plan and the teacher
blocks.text: In a math classroom the lesson plan is the line you size up a student with, to see his level and how to teach him. But the real *hiyuli* line is the teacher's own ability to create such a hierarchy for any class, to measure up any student and divide it up.

phrases.he: כך ציור הקו בחינת היולי לגבי בחינת שטח האותיות לעשותם באורך ורוחב,
phrases.en: So, too, a line is also *hiyuli* for the *shetach* of letters, to be able to write them in a length and a width.

phrases.he: כמו בחינת קוין שבאות הב' כו'
phrases.en: like the lines in the letter beis,
as explained elsewhere.

blocks.title: Three lines make an A
blocks.text: **So, too, a line is also *hiyuli* for the *shetach* of letters, to be able to write them in a length and a width.** Children learning the ABCs: "Kids, do you know how to write the ABCs?" "No." "Well, can you make a line?" "Yeah." "Well if you can make a line, then you can make the ABCs. Look, I'll show you." A line here, one here, one here, "and now you have an A." Put the same three another way and you have an N, or a Y. "You know, it's magic... Magic lines." The *Kav* is a *hiyuli* to make any letters.
The *mashal* here: **like the lines in the letter beis**. It is three lines, and the same three lines can be put together into the English letter N. **As explained elsewhere**.

sections.title: The kav hamida: the first line, short, carrying the Essence to the receivers
sections.summary: The beginning of the line goes out the smallest possible amount, only to make up and down, and so it is the *kav hamida*, the standard every measure is made from. Yet it carries all that was hidden in the point, the real light of the Essence of the giver, measured to the receivers.

phrases.en: and based on this,

phrases.he: גם ראשית המשכת הקו מן הנקודה,
phrases.en: even the first *hamshacha* of the *Kav* from the *nekuda*, coming out from the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: הגם שהוא בא בבחינת התפשטות והמשכה,
phrases.en: even though it's already *hispashtus* and *hamshacha* compared to the *Kav*,

phrases.he: אבל הוא בחינת המשכה היולית עדיין,
phrases.en: this is a *hiyuli* *hamshacha*,

phrases.he: לכלול כמה פרטי אופני המשכות לאורך ורוחב במדה
phrases.en: to include many different particular ways of bringing out to length and width in the actual *midda*,
that's why it's called the measuring line,

blocks.text: **And based on this, even the first *hamshacha* of the *Kav* from the *nekuda*, coming out from the *reshimu***, called the *reshis hakav* (the beginning of the line), only goes from up to down. It did not go out to make the whole lesson plan. It went out the smallest, infinitely small amount, and as soon as it went out at all it stopped, because it had created up and down.

That is all that was needed: the smallest thing gives a context of up and down. That concept, up and down, before and after, is reapplied over and over in all directions to make all the different things: "this one's upper, and this one's lower, and this one's righter, and this one's lefter." So the *reshis hakav* is the *hiyuli* for the whole *hishtalshelus*, breaking the *nekuda* up in all possible ways.

**Even though it's already *hispashtus* and *hamshacha* compared to the *Kav*, this is a *hiyuli* *hamshacha***, including many particular ways of drawing out length and breadth in the actual *midda* (measure), like the ruler you measure all kinds of houses with. So it can bring out anything.

**That's why it's called the measuring line**, the *kav hamida*: it is the standard of measure, just making up and down. With the smallest unit of up and down, done over and over, you can measure whatever you want.

phrases.en: and this is indicated by its shape,
it's essentially short,
it just goes from up to down.

phrases.he: אבל הוא כולל בהמשכתו על כל פנים כל מה שיש בהעלם ההיולי דנקודה כו',
phrases.en: but in this *hamshacha*, it includes, in a hidden way, everything that was hidden in the *nekuda*.
just that now it's coming out down.

blocks.title: An anything stick
blocks.text: **This is indicated by its shape**: **it's essentially short**, **it just goes from up to down**, and as soon as it went down it stopped. To measure anything you need the smallest stick. A foot stick measures 1, 2 or 100 feet; a foot and a half needs a half-foot stick, inches need inch sticks, millimeters millimeter sticks. To measure anything you need "an anything stick, which is infinitely small... It's just a something. A something can measure anything as long as it's only a something." So a *hiyuli* for measuring anything has to be just from up to down.

**But in this *hamshacha*, it includes, in a hidden way, everything that was hidden in the *nekuda*,** to bring it out in all different ways, **just that now it's coming out down**: as a teacher brings over the whole thing, but measured out to the level of the student.

phrases.he: והוא בא מכח אור העצמי הנעלם שבעצמות המשפיע שלפני צמצומו בנקודה א'

phrases.en: only that it's coming in a measured way, though. It's coming in just a line.
not coming the way that it's in the *mashpia*.

phrases.he: שהוא בהרחבת הערך של העצמות ממש
phrases.en: and that in the *mashpia*, it's totally big like the *Atzmus*.

blocks.title: The children learn the teacher's own math
blocks.text: It comes from the hidden essential light of the *mashpia* from before the *tzimtzum*. The teacher's decision to teach math is the *nekuda*; readying his *Kav* to measure up the students comes next. But what he explains is the actual math he knows. They get it in a very small, short, limited way, but it is the actual stuff from before the *tzimtzum*: "he knows 1 1 2, that's actually what he knows." The *Kav* re-extracts what was put in, as the *Gemara* is reconstituted from the *Mishna*.

**Only that it's coming in a measured way, though. It's coming in just a line**, **not coming the way that it's in the *mashpia***, where it is infinite, as broad as the *Atzmus* (G-d's essence) itself.

phrases.he: ובקו זה הנה אור העצמות בא לפי ערך המקבלים לבד
phrases.en: but in this line, it's coming only according to the *mekablim*.
nevertheless,

phrases.he: הרי יש בו מעין ודוגמת אור העצמות הנעלם בנקודה כו',
phrases.en: it does have a *maayan* and *dugma* of what was hidden in the *nekuda*,
it's just coming in a way to be brought down below,
therefore it's in the line, that it's measured and very small,

phrases.he: והוא בחינת היולי לכל אור ושפע המקבלים כו' ודי למבין:
phrases.en: And this line is a *hiyuli* for everything that comes out to the *mekablim*.

blocks.text: **But in this line, it's coming only according to the *mekablim***, the receivers, measured down to their level. If they are first graders, it is going to be "very stupid, little things compared to him."

**Nevertheless, it does have a *maayan* and *dugma* of what was hidden in the *nekuda***, a wellspring and likeness of it, because it is still really math: they understand something that he understands. **It's just coming in a way to be brought down below**.

**Therefore it's in the line, that it's measured and very small**: the line shows a finite, thin, measured revelation. As will be said later, were they on his level he would just talk straight, and nothing would be hidden; he could bring out the whole light from before the *tzimtzum* through the *Kav* again.

**And this line is a *hiyuli* for everything that comes out to the *mekablim***: the ability to limit the light and bring it out to them according to their level, in any way that fits. That is the general story of the *Kav*; the particulars come next.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the tzimtzum itself no obstacle to a revelation coming out of the reshimu, and what would a tzimtzum kipshuto look like?
Why does the point still seem to be a true tzimtzum, and what does a teacher who writes "math" on the board and walks out show?
Why will the ground not grow without a seed, and what does that teach about a hiyuli?
Why will a good student not answer your question in class, and what comes from his being a point?
What is the difference between a point and a line, and what is the whole purpose of the Kav?
Why is the beginning of the line short, and why is it called the kav hamida?

omitted.note: He reads the opening of line 43 and then repeats, word for word, the sentence on the lines of the beis and the English N (w973-1010); probably a re-recorded stretch.

notes.text: No student is heard, but in a few places he seems to answer someone: 35 w1314 ("Right, you have partial and complete tzimtzum in that way, that's like a kipshuto, yeah"), 36 w360 ("Right, exactly."), 37 w59 ("You need something connects them with, yeah"), 37 w2184 ("Yeah, well we're not talking about that kind of a point") and 35 w2054-2080 on the dot and the reshimu. With no question audible, these are kept in his voice and no question block is written.

Some phrases cite his rendering inside the explanation rather than right after the reading: line 3 (35 w174-233), line 27 (37 w2141-2151) and line 31's first phrase (38 w26-36). Line 9's second half (זהו עיקר סיבת כל גלוי ההשפעה) has no English: what follows the reading (35 w1010-1022, "All the lights in the hishtalshelus are all coming out from the reshimu") is his explanation, not a rendering of those words.

Line 12: he reads the whole line, translates its second half first ("the Kav is the opposite of this", 36 w1154-1160) and then asks "How does the Kav come out from the reshimu?" (w1168-1176), so the phrase audio is out of order.

Line 43: the English of the phrases from "even though it's already hispashtus" on comes from his second reading (39 w1341-1404). There he says "compared to the Kav" where the sense seems to be compared to the point; the phrase keeps his words.
Lines 5-6: he reads line 6's opening ("like the form of a yud") at the end of his sentence on line 5 (35 w393-401), before the alignment mark for line 6.

The remark on the Frierdiker Rebbe (37 w2757-2827), that his going up is itself a revelation and that he is going to bring down the revelation of Moshiach, is given as a mashal of "the Rebbe" and left unflagged as a Chabad teaching; a reviewer for the public edition may want to look at it.

Sources reported as he gave them: Rabbi Chaim Vital's introduction to Etz Chaim on why the Zohar was written hidden (36 w873-1134), and a letter of the Frierdiker Rebbe quoting the Rebbe Rashab in the name of the Rebbe Maharash, that Shaar HaYichud is the way into Chassidus (38 w1658-1681). Neither is checked.
Class 37 opens (w0-65) with a summary of line 13 before it reads line 14; it is placed under line 13 as a recap.
Personal details (2026-11-23): blocks that named a student, his family or the teacher's family now make the same point without the person (STYLE.md, People in the class).
